name: DegDB
tagline: Hackathon-born Go triple store that shards graph data across peers and pays nodes in bitcoin for storage.
description: DegDB, the Distributed Economic Graph Database, began as a PennApps Fall 2015 hackathon project by Tristan Rice and Chaoyi Zha. Each peer kept subject-predicate-object triples in a local SQLite file, triples were sharded across a peer-to-peer network by a murmur3 hash of the subject, and queries were JSON triple patterns sent over HTTP and fanned out to the owning shards. The 'economic' part was an incentive layer: nodes ran btcd and btcwallet so that storage and serving could be paid for in bitcoin. A planned rewrite never landed and the repository has been untouched since January 2016, so it is best read as an experiment in incentivised decentralised storage.
statusNote: Hackathon prototype (2015); no commits since January 2016.

scale.notes: Hash-sharded across peers by subject; never tested beyond development clusters.

strengths: Small, readable Go codebase showing subject-hash sharding of a triple store
Early experiment in paying peers (via bitcoin) to store and serve shared graph data
MIT licensed, so the code can be reused freely
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2016; depends on old btcd/btcwallet setups
No transactions, security model or production hardening
Query support limited to rooted triple patterns
useCases: Teaching examples of sharded triple stores
